description:
RESTATED 2026-09-03 after a fresh re-cut research pass on ca23b676f
(fz-kdt.186/183/198/192/179/184 all landed). Prototype
.kdt120/proto120-recut.diff, WIP f615f7c63. VERDICT: BLOCKED -- the cleaner
is load-bearing for a defect that is NOT this ticket's, and fz-kdt.199 owns
it.

RE-VERIFIED LIVE at ca23b676f: `@spec dbg(t) :: t when t: any` returns `any`
for dbg([]) while dbg([int]), dbg(:a), dbg({}), dbg(%{}) and even dbg([[]])
return their own type -- only a TOP-LEVEL exact `[]` fails. And
dead_closure_capture_empty_list is still a FIFO/LIFO artifact mover: main/0's
executable return is `fp[any] any` under FIFO and `fp[L] list(int)` under
LIFO, one differing backend line.

THE RULE, re-cut onto fz-kdt.184's landed polarity spine (which is the
correct fold: 184 threads BindingSide/MatchBounds and left
drop_ambiguous_empty_list_bindings polarity-blind precisely so this ticket
deletes it whole). OPENNESS is a second axis, distinct from polarity:
polarity is the DIRECTION of a bound, openness is WHETHER a covariant
occurrence contributed one. A covariant occurrence whose witness is not
ground pins no bound and OPENS the variable; an open variable instantiates
the parameter surface through close_bounds but not the RESULT (facts =
bounds minus open), so it answers Underconstrained rather than `any`. It is
an out-parameter of the single (params, args) walk fz-kdt.192 left -- no
separate pass. `[]` is GROUND, so it never opens, which is exactly why
dbg([]) = [] falls out as a fact.

MEASURED, prototype vs base: dbg([]) = [] (the Behavior-5 test flips and is
rewritten as empty_list_binding_is_a_fact, asserted STRUCTURALLY via
is_equivalent, not by a rendered string -- fz-kdt.209's rule); arrow_match
calculator unit 72/0; eleven further 184/192 pins flip, each a sound
consequence; dead_closure_capture_empty_list CONVERGES -- FIFO and LIFO
byte-identical, main/0 returning list(int) on both.

THE BLOCK (measured, not argued): deleting the cleaner moves SEVEN corpus
fixtures to WRONG ANSWERS -- 00276, 00277, 00420, enum_map_family,
enum_take_drop_split, fz_f98_range_map_converges, mailbox_closure_enum_hofs.
Enum.map, to_list, with_index and enum_map_family collapse to []. That is
the IDENTICAL set the first research pass predicted for naive
drop-deletion, so the openness axis buys ZERO corpus improvement over simply
removing the cleaner. Root cause, read off activation dumps: Enum.reduce/3
finishes through `reduce_finish({:done, a} | ..) :: a`; the first ascent
rung's argument is `{:done, []}`, so `a` binds `[]` from a GROUND witness --
openness cannot open a ground witness -- and the join-only return ladder
never re-narrows, so Enum.reverse/1([int]) types as []. A []-typed value
entering a TYPE-DISPATCHED consumer (the outer reduce in to_list/map) then
selects the empty clause and the wrong answer reaches runtime. The cleaner
was DROPPING exactly that stale binding. The difference between dbg([])
(a genuine fact) and reduce_finish({:done, []}) (a stale rung) is TEMPORAL,
and no rule local to arrow_match.rs can tell them apart.

BLOCKED BY fz-kdt.210, and NOT by fz-kdt.199 -- the coordinator's earlier
attribution to 199 was an inference from the rung's shape, and the fz-kdt.199
research REFUTED it by measurement: with 199's keying rule applied AND the
cleaner deleted, all seven fixtures still move and Enum.reverse/1([int]) still
types as []. The wrong return sits on List.reduce_cont/3[list(int),
empty_list(), a2] -- a key with NOTHING collapsed -- so no keying rule can
reach it. The measured cause is fz-kdt.210: `reduce_cont([a], b | c, ..) ::
{:done, b | c} | ..` instantiates `b|c := []` from the GROUND seed argument and
refine_call_return MEETS that contract return into the published one (`[] <:
list(int)`, so the meet is `[]`), across five call sites of which no single one
owns it. Disabling refine_call_return at all five makes the chain correct with
the cleaner deleted. Openness cannot help: a ground witness never opens, which
is exactly why this re-cut measured ZERO corpus improvement over naive cleaner
deletion. Do not attempt fz-kdt.120 again before fz-kdt.210 lands; then
re-measure whether the seven fixtures still move.

RIP-OUT WHEN IT LANDS: drop_ambiguous_empty_list_bindings and its three
helpers (~145 lines) and its call site; instantiated_match ->
instantiated_clause; the fz-f98.16 cleaner sentences in the arrow_match
module doc, addressed-arrow.md, specs.md, semantic-fixpoint.md and
externs.md (all rewritten to the openness rule in the prototype).

OPEN QUESTIONS carried for the next reviewer: should open variables be
withheld from the PARAMETER surface as well (facts-only params measured
WORSE -- 15 movers -- and contract_test.rs:403 wants the generic surface);
and X7 ([[a]] at [[]] answering Known [none]) treats a ground `none` as a
fact -- sound as a lower bound but worth an eye.

PRE-EXISTING confirmed: f(a, a) :: a at (int, []) is a FALSE Invalid at base
(the prototype fixes it, pin A8); Types::union([], [int]) interns distinct
from [int] (fz-kdt.182).

comments.text: fz-kdt.183 landed (2e0bb2706): unblocked. With proto120.diff stacked on this base, enum_map_family, enum_tier0 and fz_f98_map_reduce are byte-equal to expected and dead_closure_capture_empty_list + 00277 are FIFO/LIFO byte-identical. Handoff hazard: proto120.diff also edits .agent/docs/{externs,semantic-fixpoint,specs}.md and fixtures2/behavior/spec_shared_var_self_composition.fz, so `git checkout -- src` does not revert it. Re-cut on fz-kdt.184 (which re-cuts on 192, which waits on 198) before building.

fz-kdt.192 landed (343f3a134): open_vars(params, args) deletes -- instantiate_match already walks (params, args) once, so OpenVars becomes an out-parameter of that walk. This ticket also DELETES the empty-list cleaner, which is the real fix for D3/R20/X6: the per-parameter veto scope is now pinned as a precision loss in two places (r20_cleaner_flip_inside_one_position, x6_one_tuple_parameter_two_fields, against x6b_two_parameters_same_constraint), and 192 widened its corpus exposure from 1 row to 8. Marking ambiguity at the moment of binding removes the scope, the disagreement, and collect_ambiguous_tuple_field_vars with it. Re-cut on 184 (which re-cuts on 192).

fz-kdt.184 landed (ca23b676f): the polarity spine is in place and ready for you to fold onto. arrow_match.rs now has BindingSide { Unify, Lower, Upper } with a total flipped(), MatchBounds { lower, upper } threaded through all six collectors, and collect_arrow_match as the one reversing node. 120 re-cuts to: replace OpenVars.positive with BindingSide (it IS the polarity, measured), add OpenVars.vars (openness, the distinct axis this ticket did NOT add), and DELETE drop_ambiguous_empty_list_bindings -- which 184 deliberately left polarity-blind and inert at arrow_match.rs:585 exactly so you delete it whole. The empty-list ambiguity drop, dbg([]) = [], and dead_closure_capture_empty_list convergence are yours. Re-cut on this base (343f3a134 + 184); the old proto120.diff predates 192 and 184 and will not apply.

STACKED MEASUREMENT handed over from fz-kdt.210 (commit 89022c7cf on
wt/kdt210-build, base dd07432db). Measured by the 210 builder, not relayed.

The experiment: 210 as landed, plus a ~147-line deletion of
`drop_ambiguous_empty_list_bindings`, `collect_ambiguous_empty_list_vars`,
`collect_ambiguous_tuple_field_vars`, `is_exact_empty_list` and the single call
site in `instantiate_match`. NOTHING ELSE -- no openness axis, no
`MatchBounds.vars`. Zero build warnings. The experiment was reverted; 210 is
one commit and contains none of it.

Result vs base dd07432db, 605 fixtures:

  interp stdout+stderr (normalised)   2 movers -- the two fixtures 210 revives
  run    stdout+stderr (normalised)   2 movers -- the same two
  the seven fixtures 120 could not move (00276, 00277, 00420, enum_map_family,
    enum_take_drop_split, fz_f98_range_map_converges,
    mailbox_closure_enum_hofs)       BYTE-IDENTICAL to base on interp AND run
  canon md5 movers                    23   (120's own scope)
  executables                         5755 -- identical to 210 alone
  FIFO/LIFO canon movers, whole tree  base 2, 210 alone 2, STACKED 0
    (`dead_closure_capture_empty_list` and
     `with_index_users_keep_nested_list_elements` both converge, 5755/5755)
  `dbg([])` published return          base and 210 `fp[any] any`;
                                      stacked `fp[L] empty_list()`
  `Enum.reverse/1([int])`             `list(int)`

So both of 120's headline goals fall out of the DELETION alone. 120's openness
axis is subsumed for the RESULT half -- 210 marks wherever the walk could not
read an occurrence at all, the strictly larger set. Re-cut 120 as a deletion
and re-measure rather than carrying the axis forward.

`cargo test --lib` on the stacked tree: 1707 passed / 12 failed / 5 ignored
(debug; the release-only `metadata_macro_rejects_duplicate_keys` is red at base
too and is not in this count). Eleven are calculator re-pins 120 owns:

  tests::empty_list_binding_is_ambiguous
  contract_test::function_contract_application_treats_empty_list_witness_as_underconstrained
  pinned_verdicts::x4_mixed_arity_tuple_union_drops_the_empty_list_binding
  pinned_verdicts::x4b_same_arity_tuple_union_drops_the_empty_list_binding
  pinned_verdicts::x6_one_tuple_parameter_two_fields
  pinned_verdicts::x7_empty_list_one_level_down
  pinned_verdicts::a3_reducer_parameter_widening
  pinned_verdicts::a8_three_positions_one_variable
  pinned_verdicts::r20_cleaner_flip_inside_one_position
  pinned_verdicts::the_empty_list_cleaner_decides_which_exception_applies  <-- NEW at 210
  (the last one is 210's own seam pin: with the cleaner intact an `[]`-only
   binding is dropped from Sigma and routes into the "observed nowhere"
   exception, so the verdict is Known; deleting the cleaner leaves it in Sigma,
   it is marked, and the verdict becomes Underconstrained. 120 must flip it
   deliberately.)

The remaining two are MOVEMENTS, not re-pins, and 120's gate must justify them:

  drive_test::compiler2_dispatch_blind_escape_census_is_the_known_population
    entry plans 169 -> 171, readable 162 -> 164
  public_trace_test::analysis_claims_survive_a_run_that_could_not_re_derive_them
    fixtures2/behavior/enum_take_drop_split.fz activation claims 267 -> 271
    (+4), an fz-kdt.63 COST pin. Behaviour is unmoved and its executable count
    is unchanged at 237, but compile work rises on the arc's slowest fixture.

None of 120's 13 blocking drive_test/JIT regressions appear.

title: A @spec variable is a lower bound and a fact only when every positive occurrence contributed: the empty-list ambiguity drop goes, dbg([]) is [], and dead_closure_capture_empty_list converges
